newsitem.title: USA: FBI to work with Fed in probe of leak on rates.
newsitem.headline: FBI to work with Fed in probe of leak on rates.

text.p: The FBI has agreed to work with the Federal Reserve in investigating a leak of sensitive information about internal Fed recommendations for higher interest rates, Justice Department officials said Monday.
They said the Fed last week asked the Justice Department for FBI assistance in the inquiry being conducted under the direction of Fed Inspector General Brent Bowen and the request had been approved.

"The FBI has agreed to work with the Fed to find out what happened," one official said, adding that the inquiry would try to determine the source of the leak and whether any laws or confidentiality regulations had been violated.

The inquiry stemmed from a Reuters report on Sept. 17 disclosing that eight of the 12 district banks in the Federal Reserve System had requested an increase in the discount rate amid mounting evidence the pace of economic expansion is likely to remain brisk in the second half of 1996.
The story, written by New York-based reporter Isabelle Clary, quoted an unnamed senior Fed official. It caused bond prices to fall sharply and long-term interest rates to jump.
The disclosure came ahead of the scheduled Sept. 24 meeting of the policy-making Federal Open Market Committee to consider interest rate policy.

Fed spokesman Joseph Coyne declined comment on the reported probe, which was disclosed Monday by the Washington Post and the New York Times. "We have nothing to say," he said. Justice Department spokesman Bert Brandenburg also declined comment.
A spokesman for the U.S. Attorney's Office in Washington said, "We anticipate that if the investigation produces any evidence of criminal wrongdoing the U.S. Attorney's Office will become involved."

Another official said Justice Department prosecutors would await any evidence from the FBI and the inquiry before considering further what laws might have been violated. "It is very much up in the air," the official said. "The question is what law has been broken. They don't know."
A Reuters spokesman said the company had not been contacted by the FBI.
